thread:
inc-bot: INCIDENT 1834321000 — P1: elevated error rate on /v1/generate and potential logging of user metadata. Pager fired to #incidents and on-call. :rotating_light:
Maya S.: i'm on it, grabbing context. seeing a spike at 02:23 UTC, errors 500 from model-serving cluster. also notice a config change to debug_log_level around 02:20 by deploy-bot.
Liam (on-call): copying logs now. @Priya can you confirm whether the debug logging change could include request body fields?
Priya (SRE): quick check: the change toggled full_request_dump=true in the logging config for the staging tag that accidentally hit a subset of prod workers (bad selector). it will include request headers and body.
Maya S.: ok, mitigation plan: 1) flip config to original 2) rotate any exposed API keys 3) patch deploy filter to prevent staging tag from matching prod. 4) draft customer notification if any PII or keys leaked.
Liam (on-call): executing 1 now — flipping the flag on the fleet.
Ops-Bot: command: `platform config set logging.full_request_dump=false --selector="tag:staging AND env:prod"` — completed on 8/03 02:28 UTC.
Priya (SRE): rolling restart of affected workers started. prior logs preserved to a locked S3 bucket named `inc-1834321000-preserve` to allow investigation.
Maya S.: timeline notes: config change at 02:20, spike and 500s from 02:23—02:28, mitigation applied 02:28, restart 02:29.
Liam (on-call): we need a quick assessment: were any API keys or PII present in logs that were accessible outside core infra team? @Priya?
Priya (SRE): initial scan of the preserved logs shows multiple request headers with `Authorization: Bearer` in 21 entries and some request bodies with user email fields in 8 entries. the bucket ACLs are private; however, a third-party contractor had read-only IAM roles scoped broadly and pulled logs for debugging between 02:24–02:35.
Maya S.: that's the exposure vector. critical: identify affected customers, rotate keys where applicable, notify Legal and CS.
Jordan (Legal): please draft a scope summary. we'll need to know number of customers affected, nature of data (emails + a subset of bearer tokens), and whether tokens had long-lived privileges. Also timeline for disclosure.
Sam (CS): standing by to prepare customer outreach templates. we should avoid technical overload in initial notice. want a short statement + next steps + offer for dedicated support call.
Liam (on-call): drafting status page update — suggested short copy: `We are investigating an incident impacting API requests to /v1/generate. Mitigation in progress; some debug logs were written containing request metadata. We will notify affected customers with additional details.` Thoughts?
Maya S.: good. add ETA for next update (60 minutes). also include impacted regions (us-west-2) and that keys may need rotation.
Jordan (Legal): draft customer notice must include: what happened, what was exposed (headers with bearer tokens, email fields), scope (number of customers — TBD), actions taken (config reverted, keys rotation offered), and remediation timeline. avoid admitting irreversible compromise until full scan.
Maya S.: I'm creating a scratch customer template below. Please review and sign-off.
Maya S.: ```Hello,

We are reaching out about an operational incident affecting Redwood Inference API requests that may have resulted in limited logging of request metadata between 02:20 and 02:35 UTC on 2026-08-03. We have contained the issue and reverted the configuration that caused the logs to be written.

What happened: A configuration change intended for staging was incorrectly applied to a subset of production workers, causing detailed request data to be written to debug logs.

What information may have been included: request headers (may include Authorization tokens) and request body fields (including user email addresses in some requests).

Scope: We are actively identifying customers whose traffic appears in the preserved logs and will notify impacted accounts directly within 72 hours.

Our actions so far: the logging configuration has been reverted, affected workers restarted, preserved logs locked to a restricted bucket, and we are rotating any API credentials that appear in the preserved logs. We have also revoked contractor read access and are running a detailed audit.

Recommended customer action: rotate any long-lived API keys as a precaution. If you would like us to rotate keys for you, reply to this message and we will coordinate a guided rotation.

Next update: within 60 minutes. For questions or urgent support, contact your CS rep or reply to this message. 

We apologize for the inconvenience and are prioritizing root cause and prevention.

— Redwood Inference Trust & Security Team
```
Priya (SRE): looks fine. ops note: please add that we preserved original logs with a checksum and access logs to the preserve bucket; that's needed for audit.
Jordan (Legal): change `72 hours` to `48 hours` only if we can guarantee reaching customers that fast. can we?
Sam (CS): depends on number of affected customers. if small (<=20) CS can do targeted outreach within 24 hours. if larger, 48 hours for initial contact is reasonable.
Maya S.: current estimate after a quick grep: ~11 distinct customer API keys appear. assigning people: Sam handle customer comms, Jordan sign-off, Priya collect forensic report, Liam coordinate key rotations, Maya produce timeline + postmortem owner.
Liam (on-call): starting key rotations for the 11 keys — please expect token revocation events in the audit log. I'll post progress.
Ops-Bot: key-rotation job started: `rotate-keys --list-file=affected_keys_1834321000.csv` — job queued.
Maya S.: Sam — here's a shorter customer subject line suggestion: `Important: potential exposure of request metadata — Redwood Inference` and add a CS POC contact at the bottom.
Sam (CS): will adapt tone and prepare both short and expanded templates. Jordan, once you OK, I'll send to customers and post a status page update.
Jordan (Legal): reviewing final text now. two edits: replace "may have been included" with "may have contained" and add sentence: "We will provide confirmed details about the scope of affected data in follow-up communications."
Maya S.: applied edits; posting status page copy now. status page draft: ```Incident: Partial diagnostic logging of requests
Impact: Some API requests had request headers and bodies written to logs for a brief interval. Potential exposure of request metadata; we are investigating.
Status: Mitigation applied — reversible configuration change reverted and affected workers restarted. We are identifying impacted customers and rotating affected API credentials.
Next update: within 60 minutes
```
Liam (on-call): deployed status page update at 02:43 UTC.
Priya (SRE): final forensic note for this phase: preserved logs contain 21 Authorization header values; of those, 11 map to active customer API keys, 10 to internal/test keys. none of the bearer tokens appear to be long-lived server-side tokens (most were short TTL). full mapping uploaded to secure drive, access limited to Legal + Incident Leads.
Jordan (Legal): good. Sam proceed with sending the customer template to the 11 affected accounts, include offer to rotate keys and offer 1:1 call. cc Legal.
Sam (CS): sending now — will post confirmation here when outbound done.
Liam (on-call): rotation progress: 6/11 rotated successfully, 3 pending customer confirmation, 2 failed (retrying).
Maya S.: logging this as active incident. owners: postmortem lead = Maya, infra remediation = Priya, customer comms = Sam, legal reporting = Jordan.
Sam (CS): outbound done to 11 customers at 03:05 UTC. included both short and detailed templates and instructive steps for key rotation. one customer requested immediate rotation — coordinated with Liam and completed at 03:12 UTC.
Priya (SRE): contractor read access revoked and IAM policy tightened at 02:50 UTC. audit shows no external downloads beyond expected internal access.
Jordan (Legal): we've started preparing regulatory notification checklist; will flag if anything triggers required disclosure under applicable laws.
Maya S.: thanks team. next update planned in 60 minutes with preliminary findings. we'll keep this thread as the canonical incident record. :white_check_mark:
inc-bot: Incident 1834321000 status changed: Mitigation in progress -> Stabilized at 03:20 UTC
Liam (on-call): leaving a quick runbook snippet for postmortem: - root cause: permissive selector in deploy job - short-term fix: revert config + restrict selectors - long-term: add deploy guardrail test + automated diff on logging config - follow-ups: IAM review for contractor roles, add redaction enforcement in pipeline
Maya S.: adding timeline and action items to the incident board. closing out live paging for now, will reopen if additional impact detected.
